support.title: TAMPIQ Support
support.intro: Need help with TAMPIQ? Find answers below or contact us directly.
support.response_note: We aim to review support requests within 2 business days.

items.a: TAMPIQ helps you run protection sessions on your iPhone and review device activity related to those sessions. It is designed for personal awareness of what happens on your device while a session is active. It is not an anti-theft guarantee, spyware detector, stalker detector, emergency service, or evidence service for legal proceedings.

items.q: How do I start a protection session?
items.a: Open TAMPIQ and start a new protection session from the main flow. You can choose optional recording options (such as location) before or when you begin, depending on the permissions you have granted.

During an active session, TAMPIQ may store on-device records such as session timing, motion-related events, charging changes, app lifecycle signals, lock-related protected-data signals, and—if enabled and permitted—location snapshots. App usage summaries depend on Apple Screen Time / DeviceActivity authorization and may be shown with Apple’s time buckets. Availability of any record depends on iOS permissions and system conditions.

items.q: How do I end a protection session?
items.a: End the session from within TAMPIQ. If App Lock is enabled, the app may ask you to authenticate as the device owner before ending protection.

items.q: Can I set an automatic end time?
items.a: Yes. You can choose an automatic end time for a session. Delivery of that end depends on iOS execution and system behavior; under some conditions the session may end later than the planned time or require the app or system to resume processing.

sections.title: Protection Sessions
paragraphs: Each protection session is separated so you can review activity in context of that session only.
Operating-system limitations may affect which records are available. TAMPIQ does not claim that every possible device event will be captured.
Automatic end may depend on iOS background execution, Live Activity scheduling, and other system behavior.

sections.title: Device Activity
paragraphs: During a session, TAMPIQ may organize a timeline of supported signals such as screen/lock-related protected-data events, motion bursts, charging changes, and other device events the app is designed to observe.
These events are not guaranteed. iOS may delay, coalesce, or omit signals depending on power, permissions, and system state.

sections.title: App Usage
paragraphs: App usage information depends on iOS Screen Time / DeviceActivity capabilities and the Family Controls authorization you grant.
Some summaries use Apple time buckets. Attribution within the same hour can have limited precision.
TAMPIQ does not claim false per-second precision for app usage.

sections.title: Location Records
paragraphs: Location records are available only when you grant location permission and enable location recording for protection.
Accuracy and availability depend on iOS and system conditions. Location availability is not guaranteed.
TAMPIQ is not continuous GPS tracking. Optional modes may capture start/end snapshots or meaningful location changes when advanced recording is enabled and Always authorization is granted.

sections.title: App Lock & Privacy
paragraphs: App Lock helps keep the TAMPIQ interface private by requiring device-owner authentication (Face ID, Touch ID, or device passcode via the system).
TAMPIQ receives only success or failure of authentication. It does not receive Face ID biometric templates or images.
A privacy cover can hide app content in the app switcher. Background locking behavior follows the options you configure and iOS rules.

sections.title: Notifications & Live Activities
paragraphs: An active protection session can show a Live Activity so you can see session status at a glance.
Local notifications may remind you about auto-end or session status. Remote push delivery is not used for these session updates.
Notifications and Live Activities require system permission and can be disabled by you or limited by iOS.
Dismissing a Live Activity does not by itself stop the protection session.

sections.title: Themes & Language
paragraphs: TAMPIQ includes Light, Dark, Navy, and Colorful themes.

You can choose the app language inside TAMPIQ settings. This Help Center supports the public locales listed in the language selector, including Turkish, English (U.S.), Arabic, Traditional Chinese, French, German, Hindi, Japanese, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish (Spain), and Urdu.

sections.title: Permissions
paragraphs: TAMPIQ may request the following permissions that exist in the production app:
bullets: Motion — to detect device movement during protection.
Location (When In Use and, if you enable advanced recording, Always) — to save location records related to protection sessions.
Notifications — for local session reminders and status alerts.
Screen Time / Family Controls authorization — to show DeviceActivity / app usage summaries.
Face ID / device authentication — to unlock the app and confirm ending protection when App Lock is enabled (system authentication only).

items.a: Confirm the protection session was active, check that relevant permissions are allowed, and review whether iOS low-power or background limits applied. Not every signal is guaranteed.
Grant Screen Time / Family Controls authorization and reopen the relevant report views. Apple frameworks control what can be shown.
Enable location recording, grant the required location permission, and ensure Location Services are on in iOS Settings. Accuracy still depends on system conditions.
Allow notifications for TAMPIQ in iOS Settings. Focus modes and system limits can suppress alerts.
Confirm Live Activities are allowed for TAMPIQ, that a session is active, and that iOS has not dismissed or limited the activity.
Check whether you set an automatic end time. System scheduling and execution limits can affect exact timing.
Use your device passcode if biometric unlock fails. TAMPIQ cannot read or reset your device passcode or Face ID data.

sections.title: Bug Report
paragraphs: When you email support about a bug, please include:
bullets: iPhone model
iOS version
TAMPIQ version
Approximate time of the issue
Steps to reproduce
Screenshot if appropriate
sections.closing: Never send your Apple ID password, device passcode, TAMPIQ PIN, or other sensitive authentication secrets.

sections.title: Feature Request
paragraphs: We welcome thoughtful product ideas. Email support with “Feature request” in the subject line and a short description of the workflow you want. We read every message even when we cannot build every idea.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how TAMPIQ (“we”, “us”) processes information when you use the TAMPIQ iPhone app. It reflects the production behavior of the app: protection records are designed to stay on your device, and TAMPIQ does not operate an account system or TAMPIQ cloud backend for session telemetry.

sections.title: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: TAMPIQ is a personal protection-session app for iPhone. It helps you start and end protection sessions and review related on-device activity.
We wrote this policy to match how the shipping app works—not as generic boilerplate.

sections.title: 2. Scope
paragraphs: This policy covers the TAMPIQ iOS application and this public Help Center / Privacy Center website.
It does not cover unrelated websites or services you may open from outside TAMPIQ, such as Apple Maps when you choose to view a location.

sections.title: 3. Information TAMPIQ Processes
paragraphs: Depending on the permissions and settings you choose, TAMPIQ may process the following categories on your device:
bullets: Protection session metadata (session identifiers, start/end times, labels, configuration snapshots).
Device activity related to a session (for example motion-related events, charging changes, app foreground/background signals, and lock-related protected-data signals).
App usage / DeviceActivity summaries shown through Apple Screen Time frameworks when authorized (display may use Apple time buckets; Tampiq does not upload Screen Time rows to a Tampiq server).
Optional location records when you enable location recording and grant permission.
Preferences and settings (theme, language, retention, feature toggles).
App Lock authentication outcomes (success/failure only).
Support correspondence if you email us (processed outside the app, in email).

sections.title: 4. On-Device Processing and Storage
paragraphs: Session journals, evidence files, monitoring callbacks, preferences, and related caches are stored locally on your iPhone, including an App Group shared with TAMPIQ extensions (Activity Monitor, Activity Report, Widgets) where required for functionality.
TAMPIQ does not maintain a Tampiq account login and does not send protection session telemetry to a Tampiq application server.
If you export, share, or open content with another app (for example sharing a file or opening Maps), that action is initiated by you and follows the destination you choose.

sections.title: 5. Location Data
paragraphs: Location recording is optional and off unless you enable it and grant permission.

When enabled, TAMPIQ may store location snapshots related to protection start/end, and—if you enable advanced recording and grant Always authorization—meaningful location changes while a session is active. It is not continuous high-frequency GPS tracking.
Accuracy and availability depend on iOS Location Services and device conditions. Reverse-geocoded place labels may use Apple’s geocoding services.

sections.title: 6. App Usage / Screen Time Data
paragraphs: App usage views rely on Apple’s Family Controls / DeviceActivity / Screen Time technologies after you authorize them.
What can be shown is controlled by Apple’s frameworks and your authorization. Some values use Apple time buckets with limited same-hour precision.

TAMPIQ’s DeviceActivity monitor extension may persist schedule callback events locally for session correlation. Per-app Screen Time lists shown in sandboxed report UI are for on-device display and are not uploaded to a Tampiq server.

sections.title: 7. Permissions
paragraphs: TAMPIQ requests permissions only to provide corresponding features:
bullets: Motion — movement signals during protection.
Location — optional protection-related location records.
Notifications — local alerts about sessions.
Family Controls / Screen Time — app usage summaries.
Face ID / device owner authentication — App Lock and confirming sensitive actions via the system LocalAuthentication prompt.

sections.title: 8. Notifications and Live Activities
paragraphs: TAMPIQ uses local notifications and ActivityKit Live Activities for session status. These are not driven by Tampiq remote push servers.
You can disable notifications or Live Activities in iOS Settings. Dismissing a Live Activity does not necessarily end the underlying protection session.

sections.title: 9. App Lock / Authentication
paragraphs: App Lock uses Apple’s LocalAuthentication. TAMPIQ learns whether authentication succeeded or failed.
TAMPIQ does not receive Face ID biometric data, fingerprints, or your device passcode.

sections.title: 10. Server Transmission
paragraphs: Protection session records, evidence journals, and app preferences are designed to remain on your device.
TAMPIQ does not operate a Tampiq cloud API that receives your session telemetry, location history, or Screen Time rows.

System services provided by Apple (for example geocoding or framework authorization flows) may involve Apple’s infrastructure under Apple’s terms. Opening this Help Center website uses ordinary web hosting to deliver these pages.

sections.title: 11. Third-Party Services
paragraphs: The production iOS app’s third-party SDK dependency is Lottie (on-device animations). TAMPIQ does not integrate Firebase, Crashlytics, Sentry, advertising, or analytics SDKs in the audited production configuration.
Apple system frameworks (Core Location, Core Motion, Family Controls, DeviceActivity, ActivityKit, UserNotifications, LocalAuthentication, and related APIs) are used as provided by iOS.

sections.title: 12. Data Sharing
paragraphs: We do not sell your personal information.
We do not share protection session records with third-party advertisers or data brokers.
If you contact support by email, your message is handled for support purposes. If you share content yourself through iOS share sheets or other apps, that sharing is under your control.

sections.title: 13. Data Retention
paragraphs: In Settings you can choose how long archived records are kept: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or until you delete them (default).
When a retention period other than “until I delete” is selected, older records may be purged automatically when the app loads or resumes.

sections.title: 14. Data Deletion
paragraphs: You can delete individual sessions or clear stored records from within TAMPIQ (owner authentication may be required for destructive actions).
Deleting the app removes the app’s local container data subject to iOS behavior. Uninstall does not delete emails you already sent to support.

sections.title: 15. Support Communications
paragraphs: If you email support or privacy contacts, we process the content of that correspondence to respond to you. That email data is separate from on-device protection telemetry.
Do not include passwords, device passcodes, or TAMPIQ PINs in support emails.

sections.title: 16. Children
paragraphs: TAMPIQ is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly create accounts for children because TAMPIQ does not use an account system. If you believe a child has submitted personal information to us by email, contact us and we will delete that correspondence where appropriate.

sections.title: 17. International Users
paragraphs: TAMPIQ stores protection records on the device where the app is installed. If you use the app while traveling, those on-device records remain on that device unless you export or share them.
This Help Center is hosted on web infrastructure that may process standard technical logs needed to deliver the pages you request.

sections.title: 18. Security
paragraphs: We use reasonable technical measures appropriate for an on-device app, including App Lock options and local integrity protections where implemented.
No method of electronic storage is perfectly secure. We do not guarantee that unauthorized access can never occur on a compromised device.

sections.title: 19. User Choices and Controls
paragraphs: You can change or revoke permissions in iOS Settings, adjust retention, delete records, disable notifications or Live Activities, and change theme or language in the app.
You can also stop using TAMPIQ and remove the app from your device.

sections.title: 20. Changes to This Policy
paragraphs: We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect product or legal changes. The effective date at the top will change when we do.
Material changes will be reflected on this page. Continued use of TAMPIQ after an update means you accept the revised policy.

sections.title: 21. Contact
paragraphs: Privacy questions and support requests can be sent to the addresses shown below.
Developer / Publisher: TAMPIQ.

privacy_android.title: Privacy Policy (Android)
privacy_android.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how TAMPIQ (“we”, “us”) processes information when you use the TAMPIQ Android app. It reflects production Android behavior: protection session records and device-activity evidence are designed to stay on your device in local storage, while optional security email alerts—if you enable them and sign in—send a limited alert payload to TAMPIQ’s alert delivery service so an email can be delivered to your verified account address.

sections.title: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: TAMPIQ is a personal protection-session app for Android. It helps you start and stop a protection session and review related on-device activity for that session.
This policy is written to match how the published Android app works—not as a generic template.

sections.title: 2. Scope
paragraphs: This policy covers the TAMPIQ Android application and this public Help Center / Privacy Center website when you open Android-specific pages.
It does not cover unrelated websites or services you may open outside TAMPIQ (for example a maps app you choose after viewing a location).

sections.title: 3. Information TAMPIQ Processes
paragraphs: Depending on the permissions and settings you choose, TAMPIQ may process the following categories on your device:
bullets: Protection session metadata (session identifiers, start/stop times, labels, configuration snapshots).

Device activity related to a session (for example motion-related events, charging/power changes, app foreground/background signals from Usage Access when authorized, notification interaction signals when Notification Listener access is authorized, and lock-related signals when Device Admin is active).
Optional location snapshots when you enable location evidence and grant location permission.
Preferences and settings (theme, language, history retention, feature toggles, email-alert preferences).
App Lock authentication outcomes (success/failure only)—not your biometric templates or device PIN.
Optional cloud account identifiers used only for security email alerts and account management (Firebase Authentication user id and verified email eligibility).
Support correspondence if you email us (processed outside the app, in email).

sections.title: 4. On-Device Processing and Storage
paragraphs: Session logs, timeline events, preferences (DataStore), and related caches are stored locally on your Android device (including a local Room database).
TAMPIQ does not require a user account for core protection recording. Protection timeline history is designed to remain on the device.
If you export, share, or open content with another app, that action is initiated by you and follows the destination you choose.

sections.title: 5. Permissions and Special Accesses
paragraphs: TAMPIQ requests Android permissions and special accesses only to provide the corresponding features:
bullets: Usage Access — supported app-usage / activity signals during a protection session (when you authorize it).
Notification Listener — notification interaction signals during a protection session (when you authorize it). TAMPIQ does not use this access for advertising.
Device Admin — optional wrong lock-code / unlock-failure related signals on supported devices and Android versions (when you activate Device Admin). Capabilities vary by OEM and OS version.
Location — optional evidence snapshots when you enable location evidence and grant permission.
Notifications — local session-status notifications.
Biometric / device credential — App Lock and confirming sensitive actions via the system prompt.
Foreground service — ongoing protection monitoring while a session is active, within Android background-execution rules.

sections.title: 6. Location Information
paragraphs: Location evidence is optional and off until you enable it and grant permission.
When enabled, TAMPIQ may store location snapshots related to protection activity on the device. This is not continuous high-frequency tracking for advertising.
Accuracy and availability depend on Android location services and device conditions.

If you also enable security email alerts with a content mode that includes location, coordinates (and when available a reverse-geocoded label) may be included in the alert payload sent to TAMPIQ’s alert delivery service for that email.

sections.title: 7. Notification Access
paragraphs: With Notification Listener access authorized, TAMPIQ may record notification-related interaction signals for the active protection session on the device.
This access is for protection evidence you choose to enable—not for reading your notifications to build marketing profiles.

sections.title: 8. Device Administration
paragraphs: Optional Device Admin activation may allow TAMPIQ to observe certain lock-screen authentication failure signals on supported Android versions.
TAMPIQ does not receive your device PIN, pattern, or password content. Observability depends on Android APIs and OEM behavior; it is not guaranteed on every device.
You can deactivate Device Admin in Android system settings.

sections.title: 9. Foreground Monitoring
paragraphs: While protection is active, TAMPIQ may run a foreground service so monitoring can continue under Android’s background limits.
Android may still restrict or delay background work depending on battery optimization, OEM power policies, and system settings. TAMPIQ cannot override every OS limitation.

sections.title: 10. Optional Security Email Alerts
paragraphs: Security email alerts are optional. To use them you must sign in with a supported cloud account (Firebase Authentication / Google Sign-In where configured), verify eligibility, and opt in inside TAMPIQ settings.

When an eligible alert is sent, the Android app posts a limited JSON payload over HTTPS to TAMPIQ’s security-alert endpoint, authenticated with a short-lived Firebase ID token. The app does not embed SMTP credentials or your mailbox password.

The payload may include installation and event identifiers, session id, event type / trigger, timestamp, device name, optional risk summary fields, locale, content-mode flags, related event-type labels, and—when applicable—location coordinates. The backend resolves the recipient from your authenticated account; the device request is not designed to carry arbitrary free-form mailbox content as the transport secret.
You can choose detailed or more private email content modes where offered. You can disable email alerts, sign out, or delete your cloud account through the in-app flows when available.

sections.title: 11. Device and Installation Identifiers
paragraphs: For optional email alerts, TAMPIQ may use an installation identifier and your cloud account user id so delivery can be attributed to the correct opted-in account and deduplicated.
These identifiers are not used to sell advertising profiles.

sections.title: 12. Server Transmission
paragraphs: Core protection timeline records are designed to remain on your device.

Network transmission to TAMPIQ infrastructure occurs for optional features such as security email alert delivery, related alert-preference sync when signed in, and account deletion requests—when you use those features.
Opening this Help Center uses ordinary web hosting. Google Fonts may be loaded by the website for typography.

sections.title: 13. Third-Party Processors
paragraphs: When cloud auth / email alerts are configured in the build you install, TAMPIQ uses Google Firebase Authentication (and Google Sign-In where offered) to authenticate the optional account.
Alert delivery is performed by TAMPIQ’s HTTPS security-alert backend after authentication.
Android system frameworks (location, notifications, usage stats, device policy, biometric prompts, and related APIs) operate under Google’s and your OEM’s platform terms.

Production monitoring/analytics advertising SDKs are not described here as a required part of core local protection recording; optional Google Play services components may be present for authentication.

sections.title: 14. Data Sharing
paragraphs: We do not sell your personal information.
We do not share protection session records with third-party advertisers or data brokers for marketing.
If you contact support by email, we process that correspondence to respond. If you share content yourself through Android share sheets or other apps, that sharing is under your control.

sections.title: 15. Data Retention
paragraphs: In Settings you can choose how long archived protection records are kept on the device: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or until you delete them.
When a finite retention window is selected, older local records may be cleaned automatically during app maintenance.
Optional cloud account and alert-delivery records follow the backends that provide authentication and email delivery; you can request account deletion through the in-app account flows when available.

sections.title: 16. Data Deletion
paragraphs: You can delete individual sessions or clear stored records inside TAMPIQ (sensitive actions may require owner authentication).
Uninstalling the app removes the app’s local data according to Android behavior.
Uninstalling does not delete emails you already received or support emails you already sent.
Cloud account deletion, when available in the app, requests removal of the signed-in account via TAMPIQ’s account API.

sections.title: 17. Launcher Icon Visibility
paragraphs: TAMPIQ may offer to hide or restore its launcher icon using Android activity-alias component states.
Hiding the icon does not erase local protection records. Restoration depends on Android/OEM launcher behavior; keep a recovery path (such as settings deep link or known restore steps) before hiding.

sections.title: 18. Security
paragraphs: We use reasonable technical measures appropriate for an on-device app, including App Lock options and encrypted local stores where implemented for sensitive alert-related values.
No electronic storage method is perfectly secure. We do not guarantee that unauthorized access can never occur on a compromised device.

sections.title: 19. User Choices and Controls
paragraphs: You can change or revoke permissions in Android Settings; adjust retention; delete records; disable email alerts; sign out; deactivate Device Admin; change theme or language; and stop using or uninstall TAMPIQ.

sections.title: 20. Children
paragraphs: TAMPIQ is not directed to children under 13. We do not knowingly create cloud accounts for children. If you believe a child sent us personal information by email, contact us so we can delete that correspondence where appropriate.

sections.title: 21. International Users
paragraphs: Protection records are stored on the device where the app is installed. Optional alert authentication and delivery may involve processors that operate in multiple regions (for example Firebase Authentication).
This Help Center is hosted on web infrastructure that may process standard technical logs needed to serve the pages you request.

sections.title: 22. Changes to This Policy
paragraphs: We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect product or legal changes. When we do, the effective date above changes.
Material changes are reflected on this page. Continued use of TAMPIQ after an update means you accept the revised policy.

sections.title: 23. Contact
paragraphs: Privacy questions and support requests can be sent to the addresses listed below.
Developer / Publisher: TAMPIQ.

support_android.title: Support (Android)
support_android.intro: Need help with TAMPIQ on Android? Find answers below or contact us directly.
support_android.response_note: We aim to respond within 2 business days.

sections.title: Getting Started
paragraphs: Install TAMPIQ from Google Play, complete first-run setup, create your Tampiq PIN (not your phone PIN), and open Home to start a protection session when you are ready.
bullets: Core protection recording works on-device without a cloud account.
Optional security email alerts require sign-in and opt-in under Settings.

sections.title: How Protection Works
paragraphs: Start protection from Home using the under-track control. While active, TAMPIQ records supported signals for that session into the on-device timeline.
Stop protection from Home (owner authentication may be required). Review events under Records.

sections.title: Usage Access
paragraphs: Usage Access lets TAMPIQ read supported app-usage / activity signals during a session.
Authorize it from Protection setup or Android Settings → Special app access → Usage access. Revoking it stops those signals going forward.

sections.title: Notification Listener
paragraphs: Notification access lets TAMPIQ record notification-related interaction signals for an active session.
Enable it from Protection setup or Android notification access settings. Revoke anytime in system settings.

sections.title: Device Admin
paragraphs: Optional Device Admin may enable wrong lock-code related signals on supported devices.
Activate only if you understand Android’s Device Admin prompt. Deactivate under Android Device admin apps. Capability varies by OEM and Android version.

sections.title: Location Permissions
paragraphs: Location evidence is optional. Grant location permission only if you want location snapshots in the session timeline (and, if email alerts include location, in those alerts).

sections.title: Email Alerts
paragraphs: Optional security emails notify you about selected incidents while protection is relevant.
Sign in, verify your account email when required, opt in, choose triggers and content mode, then test from Settings if offered.
Delivery needs network access and a working backend configuration for your build.

sections.title: Background Monitoring Limitations
paragraphs: Android battery savers and OEM power managers can delay or stop background work. Prefer exempting TAMPIQ from aggressive battery optimization when you need reliable monitoring.
TAMPIQ cannot guarantee monitoring during forced stops, deep sleep modes, or after the OS kills the app process.

sections.title: Battery Optimization Guidance
paragraphs: If sessions stop unexpectedly, check Android battery optimization / autostart settings for TAMPIQ and allow unrestricted or non-optimized operation where your OEM provides that control.

sections.title: App Icon Hiding and Restoration
paragraphs: If you hide the launcher icon, remember how to restore it (in-app restore, settings deep link, or package settings) before hiding.
OEM launchers differ; if the icon does not reappear immediately, reboot or clear the launcher cache after restoring the component.

sections.title: Permission Revocation
paragraphs: Revoke Usage Access, Notification access, location, notifications, or Device Admin in Android Settings at any time. Features that depend on those accesses will stop or degrade accordingly.

items.a: Confirm battery optimization exemptions, that the app was not force-stopped, and that required accesses for your setup are still granted.
Confirm sign-in, verified email, opt-in, network connectivity, and trigger settings. Send a test email from Settings when available.
Device Admin and OEM/OS support are required for many lock-failure signals; not all devices expose the same callbacks.
Use your restore path from Settings or re-enable the Tampiq launcher component; OEM launchers may need a refresh.

sections.title: Bug Report
paragraphs: Email support with your Android version, device model, TAMPIQ version, and steps to reproduce. Do not include your Tampiq PIN, device PIN, or passwords.

sections.title: Feature Request
paragraphs: Send feature ideas to the support email. Describe the problem you want solved on Android.
